# Final Project -- Harmonic Analysis on Grid-connected Bridge Inverter (with Unipolar Modulation) {.unnumbered}

## Objective {#sec-objective}
<!-- ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->

The objective of this experiment is to design, implement, and analyse a **single-phase full-bridge inverter** in MATLAB/Simulink using **unipolar sinusoidal pulse-width modulation (SPWM)**. Specifically, the report aims to:

1. Build and verify the Simulink model with a resistive load, both without and with a filter inductor $L_f$.
2. Examine the inverter output voltage $V_{ab}$ on the resistive load and its Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) spectrum under both conditions.
3. Evaluate the voltage waveform across the resistive load and its Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) when $L_f$ is present.
4. Compare the harmonic performance of unipolar SPWM against square wave modulation.
5. Extend the model to grid-connected operation and verify the steady-state phasor relationship between the inverter output voltage, the filter inductor voltage, and the grid voltage.
6. Measure the grid current waveform and its THD.

Key simulation parameters are summarised in @tbl-params.

| Parameter | Symbol | Value |
|:--|:--:|--:|
| DC voltage input | $V_{dc}$ | 200 V |
| Fundamental frequency | $f_1$ | 60 Hz |
| Angular frequency | $\omega$ | $2\pi f_1 \approx 376.99\;\mathrm{rad/s}$ |
| Switching frequency | $f_{s}$ | 1 kHz |
| Filter inductance | $L_f$ | 1 mH |
| Resistive load | $R$ | $17\;\Omega$ |
| Peak grid voltage | $\hat{V}_g$ | $169.68\;\mathrm{V}$ |

: Simulation parameters. {#tbl-params}


## Simulink Model — Unipolar SPWM with Resistive Load {#sec-model-r}

The single-phase full-bridge inverter consists of four IGBT/diode pairs
(S1–S4) connected in two legs. In **unipolar SPWM**, the two legs are
controlled by independent sinusoidal references compared against a shared
high-frequency triangular sequence. The resulting three-level output
voltage $V_{ab}$ switches among $+V_{dc}$, $0$, and $-V_{dc}$,
pushing the dominant harmonic content to sidebands around $2f_{s}$.

### Without Filter Inductor {#sec-model-no-lf}

In this configuration the filter inductor is not included and only a resistive load is connected between the bridge midpoints. This allows the raw, unfiltered $V_{ab}$ waveform to be captured for FFT analysis.

![Simulink model with resistive load and no filter inductor (right side).
  Gate signals g1–g4 are generated by the unipolar SPWM subsystem (left side).
  The voltage measurement block probes $V_{ab}$ directly.
](images/unipolar_modulation_model.png){#fig-model-no-lf width=90%}

### With Filter Inductor ($L_f$ in circuit) {#sec-model-with-lf}

The filter inductor $L_f$ is connected in series to the
resistive load. The voltage scope is placed to measure the waveform output
of the actual load voltage after filtering.

![Simulink model with filter inductor $L_f$ added in series with the
  resistive load. The voltage scope is tapped across $R$ only.
](images/unipolar_modulation_filtered_model.png){#fig-model-with-lf width=90%}


## Output Voltage Waveform and FFT Analysis {#sec-output-voltage}

### Without Filter Inductor {#sec-fft-no-lf}

Without $L_f$, the bridge output voltage $V_{ab}$ is a three-level
switching waveform.

![Time-domain waveform of $V_{ab}$ without the filter inductor, showing
  the characteristic three-level unipolar switching pattern.
](images/unipolar_modulation_wave.png){#fig-vab-waveform width=90%}

The FFT analysis shows dominant harmonics at 60 Hz and $1000 \pm 60\;\mathrm{Hz}$. The THD level is approximately 52.3\%, a relatively high value due to the presence of low-order harmonics.

![FFT spectrum of $V_{ab}$ (no filter), obtained from the Simulink
  Powergui FFT Analysis tool. The fundamental appears at $f_1$ and the
  first significant harmonic cluster appears near $2f_{sw}$.
](images/unipolar_modulation_fft.png){#fig-fft-no-lf width=90%}

### With Filter Inductor {#sec-fft-with-lf}

With $L_f$ reconnected, the inductor acts as a low-pass filter and
attenuates the high-frequency harmonic content. The load voltage across
$R$ approaches a sinusoidal waveform.

![Voltage waveform across the resistive load with $L_f$ in circuit. The waveform is
  substantially more sinusoidal than $V_{ab}$ without the filter.
](images/unipolar_modulation_filtered_wave.png){#fig-vload-waveform width=90%}

The FFT analysis confirms that the dominant harmonic content has been shifted to higher frequencies, with the THD reduced to a much lower value of about 9\%, indicating effective filtering.

![FFT / THD analysis of the load voltage with $L_f$, from the
  Simulink Powergui FFT Analysis tool.
](images/unipolar_modulation_filtered_fft.png){#fig-fft-with-lf width=90%}

<!-- ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->
## Comparison with Square Wave Modulation {#sec-square-wave}
<!-- ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->

To benchmark harmonic performance, the gate-signal generator was replaced
with a simple square-wave source operating at the fundamental frequency
$f_1$. In this scheme, S1 and S4 conduct simultaneously during the
positive half-cycle while S2 and S3 conduct during the negative
half-cycle, producing a two-level output ($+V_{dc}$ / $-V_{dc}$) with no
carrier modulation, as shown in @fig-model-sq on the left side.

![Time-domain waveform of $V_{ab}$ under square-wave switching, showing
  the characteristic two-level pattern.
](images/square_modulation_model.png){#fig-model-sq width=90%}

The output voltage waveform is a simple square wave, and the FFT spectrum shows significant low-order harmonic content, with the harmonics of 60 Hz, 180 Hz, 
300 Hz, etc., corresponding to 1st, 3rd, 5th, etc. harmonics of the fundamental frequency. The THD is approximately 48.3\%, which is higher than that of unipolar SPWM with filtering.

![Voltage waveform across the resistive load under square-wave switching.
  The waveform is a simple two-level square wave, with significant low-order
  harmonic content.
](images/square_modulation_wave.png){#fig-vab-sq width=90%}

![FFT spectrum of $V_{ab}$ under square-wave switching, overlaid with
  the unipolar SPWM spectrum for direct comparison.
](images/square_modulation_fft.png){#fig-fft-sq width=90%}


## Simulink Model — Grid-Connected Operation {#sec-grid-model}

In the grid-connected configuration the resistive load is replaced by an
AC grid voltage source $V_g$ connected through the filter inductor $L_f$.
The inverter must synthesise an output voltage $V_{ab}$ whose amplitude and
phase are determined by the grid voltage and the desired injected current.

### Steady-State Phasor Analysis {#sec-phasor}

::: {#fig-circuit-grid}
```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}
  \draw (0,0.75) -- (0,0) -- (3,0) -- (3,0.75);
  \draw (0,1) circle[radius=0.25cm];
  \node at (0,1) {$\sim$};
  \node[left] at (-0.25,1) {$V_{ab}$};
  \draw (3,1) circle[radius=0.25cm];
  \node at (3,1) {$\sim$};
  \node[right] at (3.25,1) {$V_{g}$};
  \draw (0,1.25) -- (0,2) -- (1.1,2) arc (180:0:0.1)
                                     arc (180:0:0.1)
                                     arc (180:0:0.1)
                                     arc (180:0:0.1)
                 -- (3,2) -- (3,1.25);
  \node[above] at (1.5,2.1) {$L_f$};
  \node[below] at (1.5,1.9) {$V_{L_f}$};
  \node[below,scale=0.8] at (1,1.9) {$+$};
  \node[below,scale=0.8] at (2,1.9) {$-$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

Circuit diagram of the grid-connected inverter with filter inductor $L_f$ and grid voltage source $V_g$. The inverter output voltage $V_{ab}$ is measured across the series combination of $L_f$ and $V_g$.
:::

The KVL equation around the output loop (@fig-circuit-grid) gives:

$$
V_{ab} = V_L + V_g
$$ {#eq-kvl}

where $V_L = j\omega I_{L_f} L_f$ is the phasor voltage across the filter
inductor.

::: {#fig-phasor}
```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}
  \draw[->,thick] (0,0) -- (5,0) node[below] {$V_g=169.68\angle 0^\circ$};
  \draw[->,thick] (5,0) -- (5,1);
  \node[right] at (5,0.8) {$V_L=j\omega I_{L_f} \cdot L_f$};
  \draw[->,thick] (0,0) -- (5,1) node[above] {$V_{ab}\angle\theta$};
  \draw (1,0) arc (0:11.273:1);
  \node[right,scale=0.6] at (1,0.1) {$\theta$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

Phasor diagram showing the relationship between the grid voltage $V_g$, the inductor voltage $V_L$, and the inverter output voltage $V_{ab}$. The angle $\theta$ represents the phase lead of $V_{ab}$ over $V_g$.
:::

With the grid current $I_{L_f} = 1\angle 0°\;\mathrm{A}$ (amplitude, taken as
the reference phasor) and the circuit parameters in @tbl-params, the
inductor voltage is:

$$
V_L = j\omega L_f \, I_{L_f}
    = j \underbrace{(120\pi)}_{\omega}
      \times \underbrace{(10 \times 10^{-3})}_{L_f}
      \times 1
    \approx 3.77\angle 90°\;\text{V}
$$ {#eq-vl}

The grid voltage phasor (in phase with $I_{L_f}$ for a resistive grid
equivalent) is:

$$
V_g = 120\sqrt{2} \approx 169.68\angle 0°\;\text{V}
$$ {#eq-vg}

Because $V_L \perp V_g$ in the phasor diagram
(@fig-phasor), the required inverter output amplitude is:

$$
V_{ab} = \sqrt{V_L^2 + V_g^2}
         = \sqrt{3.77^2 + 169.68^2}
         = \sqrt{14.21 + 28\,791.38}
         \approx 169.722\;\text{V}
$$ {#eq-vab-mag}

The corresponding phase lead of $V_{ab}$ over $V_g$ is:

$$
\theta = \arctan\!\left(\frac{V_L}{V_g}\right)
       = \arctan\!\left(\frac{3.77}{169.68}\right)
       \approx 0.0222\;\text{rad}
       \equiv 1.2728°
$$ {#eq-theta}

Finally, the modulation index required to produce this output from a
$V_{dc} = 200\;\text{V}$ DC bus is:

$$
\boxed{m_a = \frac{|V_{ab}|}{V_{dc}}
           = \frac{169.722}{200}
           \approx 0.84861}
$$ {#eq-ma}

### Simulink Model Screenshots {#sec-grid-screenshots}

The sinusoidal reference amplitude and phase offset were set in the unipolar SPWM subsystem (top-left in @fig-grid-model) to match the phasor analysis results in @sec-phasor. The current measurement block was placed in series with $L_f$ to probe the grid current waveform.

![Top-level Simulink model for grid-connected operation. The series path
  from the bridge output is: $L_f$ → current measurement block → AC
  voltage source $V_g$. The current scope is a series ammeter block, not
  a parallel voltage measurement.
](images/unipolar_modulation_grid_operation_model.png){#fig-grid-model width=90%}

Waveforms were captured from the current scope, showing the grid current $i_g(t)$ in phase with the grid voltage $V_g$ for unity power-factor injection. The THD of the grid current was measured to be approximately 13\%, indicating that the inverter is effectively injecting a nearly sinusoidal current into the grid.

![Grid current waveform $i_g(t)$ (in Amphere) with $L_f$ in circuit. The waveform
  is approximately sinusoidal and in phase with $V_g$ for unity power-factor injection.
](images/unipolar_modulation_grid_operation_wave.png){#fig-grid-current width=90%}

![FFT / THD analysis of the grid current from the Simulink Powergui
  FFT Analysis tool.
](images/unipolar_modulation_grid_operation_fft.png){#fig-fft-igrid width=90%}


## Conclusion {#sec-conclusion}

This report demonstrated the simulation of a single-phase grid-connected
full-bridge inverter using unipolar SPWM in MATLAB/Simulink. The inverter was first tested with a resistive load, both without and with a filter inductor $L_f$. The FFT analysis confirmed that the filter effectively reduced the THD of the load voltage from 52.3\% to 9\%. Compared to square-wave switching, unipolar SPWM produced a three-level output voltage with dominant harmonics shifted to higher frequencies, producing a unfiltered THD of 48.3\%.

The phasor analysis in @sec-phasor showed that the inverter output voltage $V_{ab}$ must lead the grid voltage $V_g$ by a small angle $\theta \approx 1.2728°$ to drive the desired grid current $I_{L_f}$. The required modulation index was calculated to be approximately $0.84861$. The Simulink model for grid-connected operation confirmed that the grid current waveform was approximately sinusoidal and in phase with the grid voltage, with a THD of about 13\%, indicating effective harmonic performance.
